answer: Submissions that land within 133 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The whisper detector writes to tundra, and pulse exposes every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, and thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 198 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 13 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
